text:
eli: Seeing a subtle parity bug between Java and Kotlin SDKs on how per-request deadlines/cancellations are handled on Android 13+.

rhea: TL;DR?

eli: Kotlin suspend wrapper cancels coroutines and we explicitly call call.cancel() + call.timeout().cancel() which closes the socket. Java CompletableFuture path calls future.cancel(true) -> call.cancel() but the underlying OkHttp Call.timeout() isn't always cancelled, so streaming responses keep the socket open and the emulator accumulates TIME_WAIT sockets.

oscar: Stack traces / logs?

eli: repro logs: 
```
2026-02-10 12:34:21.123 W/OkHttp: response body not consumed -> connection not returned to pool
2026-02-10 12:34:21.456 W/System.err: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout
2026-02-10 12:34:21.789 I/Network: sockets open: 148 (fd limit 256)
```

mira: Interesting. How do you reproduce?

eli: Repro recipe: spawn 40 long-polling requests (server holds body for 10s), set per-request deadline 2s, cancel half from client after 1s. Kotlin wrapper: connections drop, socket count stays stable. Java wrapper: socket count climbs, some calls stuck in 'reading' state for ~10s and then close.

oscar: Can you paste the wrappers?

eli: Java (simplified):
```
CompletableFuture<Response> callAsync(Request req) {
  Call call = client.newCall(req);
  CompletableFuture<Response> f = new CompletableFuture<>();
  call.enqueue(new Callback() { ... complete f ... });
  f.whenComplete((r,e) -> { if (f.isCancelled()) call.cancel(); });
  return f;
}
```
Kotlin (simplified):
```
suspend fun callSuspending(req: Request): Response = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  val call = client.newCall(req)
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel(); call.timeout().cancel(); }
  call.enqueue(callback that resumes cont)
}
```

rhea: I think the key is `call.timeout().cancel()` which exists on OkHttp Call and explicitly clears the timeout. In Java path we only call call.cancel() which interrupts the call but doesn't always clear the per-call timeout timer created by OkHttp's Timeout class (GC doesn't close it immediately). Result: internal timer still holds reference, preventing connection from being returned promptly.

oscar: Also Java future.cancel(true) interrupts thread but for async enqueue there's no thread to interrupt; so that call path is no-op for interrupt.

mira: Workaround?

eli: Patch I tested: in Java wrapper, on cancel we call both `call.cancel()` and `call.timeout().cancel()` on the OkHttp Call instance, and also `callback.onFailure` if not already completed. That mirrors Kotlin behavior and fixed the socket leak in my soak.

rhea: Nice. Any edge cases? Calling `call.timeout().cancel()` on calls that never had a custom timeout should be safe?

oscar: OkHttp attaches an internal Timeout object per Call; cancel() is idempotent. But we should guard with try/catch to avoid surprising NPEs on older OkHttp versions. Also add a small compatibility note in docs: some older Android/OkHttp combos had slightly different timeout semantics.

mira: How about tests?

eli: Added an emulator integration test that opens 100 short-deadline long-polling requests and cancels half; assert socket count doesn't increase beyond baseline. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-java/pull/248 (WIP).

rhea: Also add a short blurb in SDK migration guide and onboarding: "When implementing CompletableFuture-based wrappers, ensure you cancel both the Call and its Timeout to fully release resources. Prefer suspendCancellableCoroutine semantics on Android."

oscar: For devex, let's include a tiny snippet in sampleapp's Java example showing the cancel + timeout-cancel pattern and link to the PR.

ci-bot: Created issue #4689: "Java SDK: ensure Call.timeout().cancel() on cancellation to avoid socket leak" - https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4689 :wrench:

mira: I'll take the PR review and add the compatibility note. Also add a lint entry in devex checklist: "When wrapping OkHttp async calls in futures, ensure timeouts are cleared on cancel."

eli: Thanks all. Leaving the thread; will update once CI passes. :thumbsup:
